records.title: Why Nespresso brought its loyalty programme back from dormancy
records.dek: Nespresso has revived its early-2000s club in the US, swapping points for rewards tied to how members engage, from barista classes to boutique visits.
summary: Nespresso has brought its dormant Nespresso Club back to the US, recasting a once-exclusive circle of home espresso owners as the backbone of its customer relationships.

Rather than offering points, the programme recognises behaviour and engagement, such as trying limited-edition flavours, joining barista classes, visiting boutiques or recycling capsules, and responds with exclusive blends and personalised offers.

Everyday perks such as recipe demonstrations and birthday gifts sit alongside an Ambassador tier with event invitations, while partnerships deliver rare experiences such as a Cannes red carpet for European VIP members.
records.why: For Retail, it shows how a mall loyalty scheme could recognise shoppers for how they take part in a visit, such as workshops, events and demonstrations, rather than for spend alone. The same logic suits Hospitality's returning guests.
records.excerpt: "We don't want to be another airline points catalog of things and stuff." - Jean-Christophe Jaunin
records.oppText: Mall loyalty members who join a seasonal demonstration or maker workshop unlock a members-only offer linked to that interest, plus an invitation to the next session.

opps.title: Recognised for showing up
opps.text: Mall loyalty members who join a seasonal demonstration or maker workshop unlock a members-only offer linked to that interest, plus an invitation to the next session.

opps.title: Learn-and-earn guest classes
opps.text: Returning guests who join a chef or barista class receive a personalised follow-up perk, such as early access to a seasonal menu, shaped by what they took part in.

opps.title: Neighbour recognition moments
opps.text: Residents who take part in recycling drives or neighbourhood events are recognised with invitations to small-group community experiences.

keyInsights: Rewarding behaviours and engagement, not spend alone, lets a brand recognise customers for who they are rather than simply because they transact.
Participatory perks such as barista classes and limited-edition flavours reward members and also tell the brand which rewards matter to them.
The core programme must stay worthwhile for every member; EY's Patricia Camden notes the best perks often remove friction rather than being expensive gifts.
Partner-led 'money can't buy' experiences can crown a programme without displacing everyday value for ordinary members.
_flags: fact-check: summary[0]: Nespresso has brought its dormant Nespresso Club back to the US (The source says Nespresso brought the Club to the U.S. this summer and revived a dormant programme. It does not say the original club previously ran in the US, so 'back to the US' is unsupported.)

_bench.title: Rewarded for How You Engage
_bench.short: Nespresso Club rewards US members with exclusive blends and personalised offers based on behaviours such as barista classes, boutique visits and capsule recycling.
_bench.lead: Instead of earning points, members are recognised for how they interact with the brand online or offline, from trying a limited-edition flavour to joining a barista class. Those signals shape the personalised rewards that follow, with recipe demonstrations open widely and Ambassador status for subscribers or heavy buyers bringing event invitations and gifts.

why.head: Recognition beyond spend
why.body: Members feel known for their interests and habits, not only for what they buy.

why.head: Participation feeds personalisation
why.body: Each class taken or limited edition tried tells the brand which rewards matter to that member.

why.head: Value at every level
why.body: Perks such as recipe demonstrations keep the programme worthwhile for members who will never reach the top tier.

transfer.how: Recognise repeat guests for joining culinary or wellness sessions and use those choices to shape offers for their next stay.
Acknowledge residents who take part in recycling or neighbourhood events with invitations to small-group community experiences.
